title.zh: 卷513 列傳三百 土司傳二 四川
title.en: Volume 513 Biographies 300: Native Chieftain Biographies 2: Sichuan
title.raw: 卷513 列傳三百 土司傳二 四川

sentences.zh: 四川邊境寥廓，歷代多設土司以相控制。

translations.literal: The borderlands of Sichuan are vast and open; through the ages many native chieftainships were established to control them.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan's frontier is broad and sparsely settled; dynasties past commonly installed native chieftains to keep it in hand.

sentences.zh: 明末，張獻忠屠蜀，石砫、酉陽、松潘、建昌等土司距險禦賊，其地獨全。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming, Zhang Xianzhong massacred Shu; the native chieftains of Shizhu, Youyang, Songpan, Jianchang, and others held the passes and resisted the bandits, and their territories alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming, when Zhang Xianzhong ravaged Sichuan, the chieftains of Shizhu, Youyang, Songpan, Jianchang, and the like held the defiles against the rebels, and their districts alone escaped destruction.

sentences.zh: 清初，戡定川境，各土司次第效順。

translations.literal: In the early Qing, when the Sichuan region was pacified, the various native chieftains submitted in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing, once the province was brought to order, the chieftains one after another pledged allegiance.

sentences.zh: 川之南有金川者，本明金川寺演化禪師哈伊拉木之後，分為大小金川。

translations.literal: South of the province there is Jinchuan, originally descended from the Ming Jinchuan Temple's Evolved Chan Master Hayilamu, divided into Greater and Lesser Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lay Jinchuan, whose line traced back to Hayilamu, the Evolved Chan Master of the Ming-era Jinchuan Temple, and which had split into Greater and Lesser Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 順治七年，小金川卜兒吉細歸誠，授原職。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shunzhi, Bu'erjixi of Lesser Jinchuan submitted in good faith and was granted his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 7 (1650), Bu'erjixi of Lesser Jinchuan came over in submission and was confirmed in his former post.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂亂後，康熙五年，其酋嘉納巴復來歸，給演化禪師印。

translations.literal: After the rebellion of Wu Sangui, in the fifth year of Kangxi, the chieftain Jianaba returned again and was given the seal of Evolved Chan Master.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Sangui's revolt, in Kangxi 5 (1666) the chief Jianaba submitted once more and received the seal of Evolved Chan Master.

sentences.zh: 其庶孫莎羅奔，以土舍將兵從將軍岳鍾琪征西藏羊峒番，雍正元年，奏授安撫司，居大金川；

translations.literal: His collateral grandson Suoluo Ben, as a native officer leading troops followed General Yue Zhongqi in campaigning against the Yangdong Tibetans, and in the first year of Yongzheng was memorialized for appointment as Pacification Commissioner, residing in Greater Jinchuan;
translations.idiomatic: A collateral descendant, Suoluo Ben, had led native troops under General Yue Zhongqi against the Yangdong Tibetans; in Yongzheng 1 (1723) he was recommended for the pacification commissionership and established himself in Greater Jinchuan;

sentences.zh: 而舊土司澤旺居小金川，莎羅奔以女阿扣妻澤旺。

translations.literal: while the former native chieftain Zewang dwelt in Lesser Jinchuan; Suoluo Ben gave his daughter A'kou in marriage to Zewang.
translations.idiomatic: while the former chieftain Zewang remained in Lesser Jinchuan, Suoluo Ben marrying his daughter A'kou to him.

sentences.zh: 澤旺懦，為妻所制。

translations.literal: Zewang was timid and controlled by his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Zewang was weak-willed and ruled by his wife.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十一年，莎羅奔劫澤旺去，奪其印。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Qianlong, Suoluo Ben seized Zewang and carried him off, taking his seal.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 11 (1746), Suoluo Ben abducted Zewang and seized his official seal.

sentences.zh: 十二年，又攻革布希劄及明正兩土司。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he again attacked the two native chieftainships of Gebuxizha and Mingzheng.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he attacked the Gebuxizha and Mingzheng chieftainships as well.

sentences.zh: 朝廷調張廣泗總督四川，進駐澤旺所居美諾官寨，而以其弟良爾吉從征。

translations.literal: The court transferred Zhang Guangsi to be governor-general of Sichuan; he advanced and encamped at the Meinuo official stockade where Zewang dwelt, and took Zewang's younger brother Liang'erji on campaign with him.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Zhang Guangsi governor-general of Sichuan. He moved up to Zewang's seat at Meinuo and brought Zewang's younger brother Liang'erji along on the expedition.

sentences.zh: 時莎羅奔居勒烏圍，其兄子郎卡居噶爾厓，地在大金川河東，而河西亦有地數百里。

translations.literal: At that time Suoluo Ben dwelt at Lewuwei, and his brother's son Langka at Ga'erya; the land lay east of the Greater Jinchuan River, yet west of the river there were also several hundred li of territory.
translations.idiomatic: Suoluo Ben held Lewuwei while his nephew Langka held Ga'erya on the east bank of the Greater Jinchuan River, with hundreds of li of domain on the west bank as well.

sentences.zh: 廣泗調兵三萬，一路出川西攻河東，一路出川南攻河西。

translations.literal: Guangsi mobilized thirty thousand troops: one route out of western Sichuan to attack east of the river, one route out of southern Sichuan to attack west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi assembled thirty thousand men, one column marching from western Sichuan against the east bank and another from the south against the west bank.

sentences.zh: 而河東一路又分為四，以兩路攻勒烏圍，以兩路攻噶爾厓，河西亦分兩路，攻庚特額諸山，刻期蕆事。

translations.literal: The eastern route was further divided into four: two columns against Lewuwei, two against Ga'erya; west of the river was also split into two, to attack the mountains of Gengte'e and the rest, with a fixed date to finish the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern force split four ways—two against Lewuwei, two against Ga'erya—while the western force divided in two to strike the Gengte'e hills, all on a set schedule to bring the campaign to a close.

sentences.zh: 阻險不前，上命大學士公訥親往視師，起嶽鍾琪於廢籍。

translations.literal: Blocked by difficult terrain they did not advance; the emperor ordered Grand Secretary Duke Neqin to go inspect the army, and restored Yue Zhongqi from disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Stalled by the terrain, the court sent Grand Secretary Duke Neqin to take charge of the army and recalled Yue Zhongqi from retirement.

sentences.zh: 鍾琪與廣泗議定，自任由黨壩取勒烏圍，而廣泗由昔嶺取噶爾厓。

translations.literal: Zhongqi and Guangsi agreed that Zhongqi himself would take the Dangba route to seize Lewuwei, while Guangsi would take Xiling to seize Ga'erya.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqi and Guangsi agreed that Zhongqi would advance via Dangba on Lewuwei while Guangsi moved through Xiling against Ga'erya.

sentences.zh: 會訥親至，下令限三日克噶爾厓，總兵任舉、參將買國良戰死。

translations.literal: When Neqin arrived he ordered Ga'erya taken within three days; Regional Commander Ren Ju and Assistant Commander Mai Guoliang died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Neqin arrived he gave a three-day deadline for taking Ga'erya; Regional Commander Ren Ju and Assistant Commander Mai Guoliang were killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 廣泗輕訥親不知兵，而惡其淩己，故飾推讓，實以困之，軍中解體。

translations.literal: Guangsi looked down on Neqin as ignorant of warfare and resented his domineering manner, so he feigned deference while in fact hampering him, and the army fell apart.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi despised Neqin as a civilian amateur and resented his high-handedness; he made a show of yielding while actually obstructing him, and morale in the ranks collapsed.

sentences.zh: 良爾吉夙與阿扣通，莎羅奔因使成配，倚作間諜，官軍動息輒為所備。

translations.literal: Liang'erji had long been intimate with A'kou; Suoluo Ben therefore had them paired and relied on them as spies, so the government army's every move was known in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Liang'erji had long carried on with A'kou; Suoluo Ben encouraged the affair and used them as spies, so the rebels were forewarned of every government move.

sentences.zh: 師久無功，上怒甚，會訥親劾廣泗，於是逮廣泗入京，而命大學士傅恆為經略，代訥親。

translations.literal: The army long achieved nothing; the emperor was greatly angered. Neqin impeached Guangsi, whereupon Guangsi was arrested and brought to the capital, and Grand Secretary Fu Heng was appointed campaign director in Neqin's place.
translations.idiomatic: After months without victory the emperor's wrath was fierce. Neqin impeached Guangsi, who was arrested and sent to the capital; Grand Secretary Fu Heng was appointed to replace him as campaign director.

sentences.zh: 冬，殺廣泗，賜訥親死。

translations.literal: In winter Guangsi was executed and Neqin was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Guangsi was put to death and Neqin was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 十二月，傅恆至軍，斬良爾吉、王秋、阿扣以斷內應。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Fu Heng reached the army and beheaded Liang'erji, Wang Qiu, and A'kou to cut off internal collusion.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Fu Heng reached headquarters and executed Liang'erji, Wang Qiu, and A'kou to sever the rebels' inside contacts.

sentences.zh: 十四年春正月，奏言：「金川之事，臣到軍以來，始知本末。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the fourteenth year he memorialized: 'As to the affair of Jinchuan, only since I reached the army have I come to know how it began and how it stands.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianlong 14 (1749) he memorialized: 'Concerning Jinchuan, only since I joined the army have I grasped how the matter began and where it stands.

sentences.zh: 當紀山進討之始，惟馬良柱轉戰直前，逾沃日，收小金川，直抵丹噶，其鋒甚銳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jishan's advance, only Ma Liangzhu fought straight ahead, crossed Wori, recovered Lesser Jinchuan, and pressed on to Danga; his momentum was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: When Jishan first marched in, only Ma Liangzhu drove straight forward, crossed Wori, recovered Lesser Jinchuan, and pushed on to Danga with tremendous momentum.

sentences.zh: 其時張廣泗若速濟師策應，乘賊守備未周，殄滅尚易；

translations.literal: Had Zhang Guangsi at that time swiftly brought up troops in support, while the rebels' defenses were not yet complete, extermination would still have been easy;
translations.idiomatic: Had Zhang Guangsi hurried reinforcements forward while the rebels' defenses were still thin, wiping them out would have been straightforward;

sentences.zh: 乃坐失機會，宋宗璋逗留於雜谷，許應虎失機於的郊，致賊得盡據險要，增碉備禦，七路、十路之兵無一路得進。

translations.literal: instead he sat by and lost the opportunity; Song Zongzhang lingered at Zagu, Xu Yinghu missed his chance at Dijiao, so the rebels came to hold all the strategic points, added blockhouses for defense, and of the troops on seven routes and ten routes not one route could advance.
translations.idiomatic: instead the chance was wasted: Song Zongzhang stalled at Zagu and Xu Yinghu lost his opening at Dijiao, allowing the rebels to seize every strong point, throw up blockhouses, and block every one of the seven or ten columns sent against them.

sentences.zh: 及訥親至軍，嚴切催戰，任舉敗歿，銳挫氣索，晏起偷安，一以軍務委張廣泗。

translations.literal: When Neqin reached the army he urged battle sternly; Ren Ju was defeated and killed, keenness was blunted and spirit exhausted; he rose late and sought ease, leaving all military affairs to Zhang Guangsi.
translations.idiomatic: When Neqin arrived he pressed for action; Ren Ju's defeat broke the army's spirit, and Neqin himself rose late and sought comfort, leaving everything to Zhang Guangsi.

sentences.zh: 廣泗又聽奸人所愚，惟恃以卡逼卡、以碉逼碉之法，槍砲惟及堅壁，於賊無傷，而賊不過數人，從暗擊明，槍不虛發，是我惟攻石，而賊實攻人。

translations.literal: Guangsi again listened to villains' deceit and relied solely on the method of pressing stockade against stockade and blockhouse against blockhouse; muskets and cannon reached only the solid walls and did the rebels no harm, while the rebels were but a few men, striking from darkness at light, every shot finding its mark—we were only attacking stone, while the rebels were truly attacking men.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi, misled by bad counsel, relied on driving stockade against stockade and tower against tower; cannon fire battered stone walls without touching the defenders, while a handful of rebels fired from cover into the open with deadly accuracy—we were battering stone while they were killing men.

sentences.zh: 且於碉外開壕，兵不能越，而賊得伏其中自下擊上。

translations.literal: Moreover they dug trenches outside the blockhouses so troops could not cross, while the rebels could lie in wait therein and strike from below upward.
translations.idiomatic: They dug trenches around the towers so our men could not cross, while the rebels lay in wait below to shoot upward.

sentences.zh: 又戰碉銳立，高於中土之塔，建造甚巧，數日可成，隨缺隨補，頃刻立就。

translations.literal: Moreover their war towers stood sharp and tall, higher than towers in the central provinces, built with great skill; in a few days they could be completed, repaired as soon as damaged, erected in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: Their fighting towers rose higher than any tower in China proper, ingeniously built in days and rebuilt the moment one fell.

sentences.zh: 且人心堅固，至死不移，碉盡碎而不去，砲方過而人起，主客勞佚，形勢迥殊，攻一碉難於克一城。

translations.literal: Moreover their hearts were firm and unshaken unto death; though a tower was shattered they would not leave; the moment cannon fire passed they rose again; host and guest differed in toil and rest, the situation was utterly unlike—taking one tower was harder than storming a city.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders' resolve was iron; they would not quit even when a tower was smashed, and rose again the moment our cannon fire lifted. We wore ourselves out while they rested at ease—capturing a single tower was harder than taking a walled city.

sentences.zh: 即臣所駐卡撒山頂，已有三百餘碉，計半月旬日得一碉，非數年不能盡。

translations.literal: Even on the summit of Kasashan where your servant is stationed there are already more than three hundred towers; reckoning half a month or ten days per tower, several years would not suffice to finish them.
translations.idiomatic: On Kasashan alone, where I am encamped, there are already more than three hundred towers; at half a month or ten days per tower, years would be required to reduce them all.

sentences.zh: 且得一碉輒傷數十百人，較唐人之攻石峰堡，尤為得不償失。

translations.literal: Moreover for each tower taken several tens or hundreds of men were wounded—compared with the Tang attack on Shifeng Fortress, the gain was even less worth the cost.
translations.idiomatic: Each tower cost us dozens or hundreds of casualties—a worse bargain even than the Tang siege of Shifeng Fortress.

sentences.zh: 惟有使賊失其所恃，而我兵乃得展其所長。

translations.literal: Only by making the rebels lose what they rely on can our troops then display their strengths.
translations.idiomatic: We must deprive the enemy of what they rely on before our troops can fight to their advantage.

sentences.zh: 臣擬俟大兵齊集，別選銳師，旁探間道，裹糧直入，逾碉勿攻，繞出其後，即以圍碉之兵作為護餉之兵。

translations.literal: Your servant proposes to wait until the main forces are assembled, then select elite troops, probe side paths, enter carrying provisions, pass the towers without attacking, circle behind them, and use the troops besieging the towers as escorts for supplies.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that when the main army is assembled we detach elite columns to find hidden routes, march in with pack provisions, bypass the towers without assaulting them, and turn the troops now tied down before the towers into escorts for our supply lines.

sentences.zh: 番眾無多，外備既密，內守必虛。

translations.literal: The barbarian masses are not numerous; with outer defenses already dense, inner defense must be weak.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen are few in number; with their outer defenses stretched thin, the interior must be poorly guarded.

sentences.zh: 我兵即從捷徑搗入，則守碉之番各懷內顧，人無固志，均可不攻自潰。

translations.literal: If our troops then strike in by the swift path, the barbarians guarding the towers will each fear for what lies behind, men will lack firm will, and all can collapse without being attacked.
translations.idiomatic: If we strike in by a fast route, the tower garrisons will fear for their homes, lose heart, and collapse without a fight.

sentences.zh: 至於奮勇固仗滿兵，而鄉導必用土兵，土兵中小金川尤驍勇。

translations.literal: As for bold fighting, one must rely on Manchu troops, but guides must be native soldiers; among native soldiers those of Lesser Jinchuan are especially fierce and brave.
translations.idiomatic: Bold assaults must rely on Manchu troops, but guides must be native levies—and among them the men of Lesser Jinchuan are the fiercest.

sentences.zh: 今良爾吉之奸諜已誅，澤旺與賊仇甚切，驅策用之，自可得力。

translations.literal: Now that Liang'erji's treacherous spying has been punished by death, Zewang bears a very keen grudge against the rebels; drive and use him and strength can naturally be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: With Liang'erji's treachery ended, Zewang's hatred of the rebels can be turned to good account if we press him into service.

sentences.zh: 至沃日、瓦寺兵強而少，雜棱、綽斯甲等兵眾而懦。

translations.literal: As for Wori and Wasi, their troops are strong but few; Zaling, Chuosijia, and the like have many troops but are timid.
translations.idiomatic: Wori and Wasi field strong but small contingents; Zaling, Chuosijia, and similar chieftains have numbers but little fight in them.

sentences.zh: 明正、木坪忠順有餘，強悍不足。

translations.literal: Mingzheng and Muping have loyalty in surplus but fierceness in deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzheng and Muping are loyal enough but not fierce enough.

sentences.zh: 革什乍兵銳，可當一路。

translations.literal: The troops of Geshizha are sharp and can hold one route.
translations.idiomatic: Geshizha's warriors are keen and can take a column on their own.

sentences.zh: 是各土司環攻分地之說雖不可恃，而未嘗不可資其兵力。

translations.literal: Thus although the plan of having each native chieftain encircle and attack in separate territories cannot be relied on, one may yet draw on their military strength.
translations.idiomatic: The scheme of having every chieftain invest separate districts cannot be counted on, but their forces can still be used to advantage.

sentences.zh: 臣決計深入，不與爭碉，惟俟四面佈置，出其不意，直搗巢穴，取其渠魁，定於四月間報捷。

translations.literal: Your servant is resolved to penetrate deeply, not contend over towers, only wait until arrangements on all four sides are made, take them unawares, strike straight at the nest, seize their ringleaders, and fix victory in report for the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: I am resolved to push deep inland without fighting for every tower, deploy on all sides, take them by surprise, strike their stronghold, seize the leaders, and report victory by the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 」上屢奉皇太后息武寧邊之諭，命傅恆班師。

translations.literal: ' The emperor repeatedly received the Empress Dowager's instruction to cease warfare and pacify the borderlands, and ordered Fu Heng to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor had repeatedly received the Empress Dowager's counsel to cease fighting and pacify the frontier, and ordered Fu Heng to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 時傅恆及鍾琪兩路連克碉卡，軍聲大振，莎羅奔乞降於鍾琪，鍾琪輕騎徑赴其巢，賊大感動，頂佛經立誓聽約束。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Heng and Zhongqi on two routes took tower and stockade after tower and stockade in succession; military prestige rose greatly. Suoluo Ben begged to surrender to Zhongqi; Zhongqi with light cavalry went straight to his nest; the rebels were deeply moved, bore the Buddhist sutra on their heads and swore to obey terms.
translations.idiomatic: By then Fu Heng and Zhongqi were sweeping tower after tower on both fronts, and morale soared. Suoluo Ben sued for peace through Zhongqi, who rode lightly straight to the rebel stronghold; deeply moved, the rebels swore on the Buddhist scriptures to submit.

sentences.zh: 次日，鍾琪率莎羅奔父子坐皮船出洞詣大軍，莎羅奔等叩顙，誓遵六事，歸各土司侵地，獻凶酋，納軍械，歸兵民，供徭役。

translations.literal: The next day Zhongqi led Suoluo Ben and his son and grandson in leather boats out of the cave to the great army; Suoluo Ben and the others kowtowed, swearing to observe six conditions: return lands seized from each native chieftain, present the murderous chiefs, surrender military equipment, return soldiers and civilians, and supply corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhongqi brought Suoluo Ben and his kin out by skin boat to the main camp. They kowtowed and pledged six terms: restore seized chieftain lands, hand over rebel leaders, surrender arms, return captives, and furnish labor service.

sentences.zh: 乃宣詔赦其死。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was proclaimed pardoning their death.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then read pardoning them from death.

sentences.zh: 諸番焚香作樂，獻金佛謝。

translations.literal: The various tribes burned incense and made music, presenting a golden Buddha in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen burned incense, made music, and presented a golden Buddha in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 二月，捷聞，詔賞傅恆、鍾琪等。

translations.literal: In the second month news of victory arrived; an edict rewarded Fu Heng, Zhongqi, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month victory was reported and Fu Heng, Zhongqi, and their colleagues were rewarded by edict.

sentences.zh: 既而莎羅奔兄子郎卡主土司事，漸桀驁。

translations.literal: Afterward Suoluo Ben's brother's son Langka took charge of the native chieftainship and gradually grew arrogant and defiant.
translations.idiomatic: Suoluo Ben's nephew Langka then assumed the chieftainship and grew increasingly unruly.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，逐澤旺及革布希劄土司。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he drove out Zewang and the Gebuxizha native chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 23 (1758) he expelled Zewang and the Gebuxizha chieftain.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，詔四川總督阿勒泰檄九土司環攻之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year an edict ordered Sichuan Governor-General Aletai to dispatch the nine native chieftains in encircling attack.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 31 (1766) the court ordered Governor-General Aletai of Sichuan to mobilize nine chieftains for a joint siege.

sentences.zh: 九土司者，巴旺、丹壩、沃日、瓦寺、綽斯甲布、明正、木坪、革布希乍及小金川也。

translations.literal: The nine native chieftains were Bawang, Danba, Wori, Wasi, Chuosijiabu, Mingzheng, Muping, Gebuxizha, and Lesser Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The nine were Bawang, Danba, Wori, Wasi, Chuosijiabu, Mingzheng, Muping, Gebuxizha, and Lesser Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 巴旺、丹壩皆彈丸，非金川敵。

translations.literal: Bawang and Danba were both mere pellets and no match for Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bawang and Danba were tiny domains and no match for Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 明正、瓦寺形勢阻隔，其力足制金川。

translations.literal: Mingzheng and Wasi were separated by terrain and configuration; their strength was sufficient to restrain Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzheng and Wasi, though separated by terrain, had strength enough to check Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 而地相逼者，莫如綽斯甲布與小金川。

translations.literal: Yet of those whose lands pressed close, none were like Chuosijiabu and Lesser Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains whose lands bordered Jinchuan most closely were Chuosijiabu and Lesser Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 阿勒泰不知離其黨與，反聽兩金川釋仇締約，自是狼狽為奸，諸小土司咸不敢抗。

translations.literal: Aletai did not know to separate their factions; on the contrary he allowed the two Jinchuans to release enmity and conclude a pact, whereupon they aided each other in villainy, and the lesser native chieftains all dared not resist.
translations.idiomatic: Aletai failed to drive a wedge between them and instead let Greater and Lesser Jinchuan reconcile and ally; from then on they worked hand in glove, and the smaller chieftains dared not stand up to them.

sentences.zh: 時澤旺老病不問事，郎卡亦旋死，其子索諾木與僧格桑侵鄂克什土司地。

translations.literal: At that time Zewang was old and ill and paid no heed to affairs; Langka also soon died, and his son Suonuomu together with Senggesang encroached on the territory of the E'keshi native chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Zewang was aged and infirm and took no part in affairs; Langka soon died as well, and his son Suonuomu with Senggesang encroached on E'keshi territory.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，索諾木誘殺革布希劄土官，而僧格桑再攻鄂克什及明正土司，與官軍戰。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year Suonuomu lured and killed the Gebuxizha native official, while Senggesang again attacked the E'keshi and Mingzheng native chieftains and fought the government army.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 36 (1771) Suonuomu treacherously killed the Gebuxizha chieftain, while Senggesang again attacked E'keshi and Mingzheng and clashed with government troops.

sentences.zh: 上以前此出師，本以救小金川。

translations.literal: The emperor said that the previous dispatch of troops had originally been to rescue Lesser Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor observed that the earlier campaign had been mounted to save Lesser Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 今小金川反悖逆，罪不赦。

translations.literal: Now Lesser Jinchuan has in turn rebelled and been disloyal; the crime cannot be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser Jinchuan had now turned rebel in its turn, a crime beyond pardon.

sentences.zh: 賜阿勒泰死，命大學士溫福自雲南赴四川，以尚書桂林為四川總督，共討賊。

translations.literal: Aletai was granted death; Grand Secretary Wenfu was ordered from Yunnan to Sichuan, and Minister Guilin was made governor-general of Sichuan to join in attacking the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Aletai was ordered to take his own life; Grand Secretary Wenfu was sent from Yunnan to Sichuan and Minister Guilin appointed governor-general to join the campaign against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 溫福由汶川出西路，桂林由打箭爐出南路。

translations.literal: Wenfu marched out the western route from Wenchuan; Guilin marched out the southern route from Dajianlu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu advanced from Wenchuan on the western route and Guilin from Dajianlu on the south.

sentences.zh: 僧格桑求援於索諾木，索諾木潛兵助之。

translations.literal: Senggesang sought aid from Suonuomu; Suonuomu secretly sent troops to help him.
translations.idiomatic: Senggesang appealed to Suonuomu, who sent troops to his aid in secret.

sentences.zh: 三十七年春，桂林克復革布希劄土司故地，溫福克資里及阿喀。

translations.literal: In spring of the thirty-seventh year Guilin recovered the former territory of the Gebuxizha native chieftain; Wenfu took Zili and Aka.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qianlong 37 (1772) Guilin recovered Gebuxizha's former domain and Wenfu took Zili and Aka.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以阿桂為參贊大臣，代桂林赴南路。

translations.literal: The court appointed Agui as participating minister, replacing Guilin on the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: Agui was appointed participating minister to replace Guilin on the southern front.

sentences.zh: 十一月，阿桂以皮船宵濟，連奪險隘，直搗賊巢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Agui crossed by night in leather boats, took strategic passes in succession, and struck straight at the rebel nest.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Agui crossed by night in skin boats, seized pass after pass, and drove straight for the rebel stronghold.

sentences.zh: 十二月，軍抵美諾，進至底木達，俘澤旺，檄索諾木縛獻僧格桑，不應。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the army reached Meinuo, advanced to Dimuda, captured Zewang, and dispatched a summons to Suonuomu to bind and present Senggesang; he did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the army reached Meinuo and pushed on to Dimuda, capturing Zewang and demanding that Suonuomu hand over Senggesang bound; he refused.

sentences.zh: 上命溫福為定邊將軍，阿桂、豐伸額為副將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Wenfu Pacification Commissioner of the Border, with Agui and Fengshen'e as deputy commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu was named Pacification Commissioner of the Border with Agui and Fengshen'e as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 溫福、阿桂奏六路進兵之策。

translations.literal: Wenfu and Agui memorialized a plan for advance on six routes.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu and Agui proposed a six-column advance.

sentences.zh: 溫福由功噶入，阿桂由當噶入，豐伸額由綽斯甲布入。

translations.literal: Wenfu entered by Gongga, Agui by Dangga, Fengshen'e by Chuosijiabu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu would enter via Gongga, Agui via Dangga, and Fengshen'e via Chuosijiabu.

sentences.zh: 三十八年春，溫福以賊扼險不得進，別取道攻昔嶺，駐營木果木，令提督董天弼分屯底木達，守小金川之地。

translations.literal: In spring of the thirty-eighth year Wenfu, because the rebels held the passes and he could not advance, took another route to attack Xiling, encamped at Muguomu, and ordered Provincial Commander Dong Tianbi to divide forces and garrison Dimuda, guarding the territory of Lesser Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qianlong 38 (1773) Wenfu, blocked by the rebels in the passes, swung toward Xiling and encamped at Muguomu, leaving Provincial Commander Dong Tianbi at Dimuda to hold Lesser Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 溫福為人剛愎，不廣諮方略，惟襲廣泗故智，以碉卡逼碉卡，建築千計。

translations.literal: Wenfu was obstinate by nature, did not widely consult on strategy, and only followed Guangsi's old trick of pressing tower and stockade against tower and stockade, building by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu was stubborn and rarely sought counsel; he merely repeated Guangsi's tactic of tower against tower, throwing up thousands of blockhouses.

sentences.zh: 初索諾木欲並小金川地，故留僧格桑挾以號召。

translations.literal: At first Suonuomu wished to annex the territory of Lesser Jinchuan, so he kept Senggesang to wield as a rallying cry.
translations.idiomatic: Suonuomu had wanted to absorb Lesser Jinchuan and kept Senggesang as a figurehead to rally support.

sentences.zh: 六月，陰遣小金川頭目等由美諾溝出煽故降番使復叛。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he secretly sent Lesser Jinchuan chiefs and others out through the Meinuo ravine to incite formerly surrendered tribes to rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he secretly sent Lesser Jinchuan leaders through the Meinuo gorge to stir up formerly subdued tribes into revolt.

sentences.zh: 諸番見大軍久頓，蜂起應之，攻陷天弼營，遂劫糧台，潛兵襲木果木，奪砲局，斷汲道，賊四面蹂入大營，溫福死之，將士隨員死者數十人，各卡兵望風潰。

translations.literal: The tribes, seeing the great army long stalled, rose like bees to answer; they stormed Tianbi's camp, then plundered the grain depot, sent troops in secret to strike Muguomu, seized the artillery park, cut the water route; rebels trampled in on all four sides into the great camp; Wenfu died; officers and soldiers who followed him numbered several tens dead; troops at each stockade fled at the mere sight of wind.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the main army bogged down, the tribes rose everywhere, overran Tianbi's camp, looted the supply depot, and fell on Muguomu by surprise, seizing the artillery park and cutting off the water supply. Rebels poured into the main camp from all sides; Wenfu was killed along with dozens of his staff, and garrisons along the line collapsed without a fight.

sentences.zh: 海蘭察聞警赴援，殿眾由間道退出，收集潰卒，尚萬數千人，其戰歿者三千餘，小金川地復陷。

translations.literal: Hailancha, hearing the alarm, went to aid; he covered the rear as the host withdrew by a hidden path, gathered scattered troops, and still had several tens of thousands of men; those killed in battle were more than three thousand; the territory of Lesser Jinchuan fell again.
translations.idiomatic: Hailancha rushed to the rescue, covered the retreat along a back trail, and rallied the fugitives—still some ten thousand men, though more than three thousand had fallen and Lesser Jinchuan was lost again.

sentences.zh: 惟阿桂一軍屹然不動，乃整隊出屯翁古爾壟。

translations.literal: Only Agui's army stood firm unmoved; he then re-formed his ranks and went out to encamp at Wenggu'erlong.
translations.idiomatic: Only Agui's column held firm; he re-formed his troops and withdrew to encamp at Wenggu'erlong.

sentences.zh: 上在熱河聞報，召大學士劉統勳詣行在咨之。

translations.literal: The emperor at Rehe heard the report and summoned Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun to the traveling palace for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: At his summer retreat in Rehe the emperor heard the news and summoned Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun for counsel.

sentences.zh: 統勳前言金川不必勞師，至是亦主用兵。

translations.literal: Tongxun had earlier said Jinchuan did not require troubling the army; by this time he also advocated using troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tongxun had once argued that Jinchuan did not warrant a major campaign; now he too urged continued military action.

sentences.zh: 乃授阿桂定西將軍，豐伸額、明亮為副將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Agui was appointed Pacification General of the West, with Fengshen'e and Mingliang as deputy commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Agui was named Pacification General of the West, with Fengshen'e and Mingliang as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 十月，阿桂改赴西路，明亮赴南路。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Agui shifted to the western route and Mingliang to the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Agui moved to the western front and Mingliang to the south.

sentences.zh: 豐伸額仍由綽斯甲布進取宜喜，阿桂入自鄂克什，轉戰五晝夜，直抵美諾，克之；

translations.literal: Fengshen'e still advanced from Chuosijiabu to take Yixi; Agui entered from E'keshi, fought for five days and nights, pressed straight to Meinuo, and took it;
translations.idiomatic: Fengshen'e pressed on from Chuosijiabu toward Yixi while Agui entered from E'keshi, fought five days and nights without rest, and stormed Meinuo;

sentences.zh: 明亮入自瑪爾裏，所向皆捷，遂盡復小金川地。

translations.literal: Mingliang entered from Ma'erli, victorious wherever he went, and thus fully recovered the territory of Lesser Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mingliang advanced from Ma'erli with uninterrupted success and fully recovered Lesser Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 惟大金川自十二三年以來，全力抗守，增壘設險，嚴密十倍小金川。

translations.literal: Only Greater Jinchuan since the twelfth and thirteenth years had resisted with full strength, added ramparts and set barriers, ten times as tight as Lesser Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Greater Jinchuan alone, since the first campaign of the 1740s, had resisted with all its strength, fortifying its defenses to a degree ten times that of Lesser Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 七月，令諸軍分攻各碉寨，數十道並進。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he ordered the armies to attack each tower and stockade separately, several tens of columns advancing together.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he ordered columns to assault the towers and stockades on dozens of fronts at once.

sentences.zh: 海蘭察率死士六百削壁猱引而上，趾頂相接，比明及其碉，一湧入，盡殲守賊。

translations.literal: Hailancha led six hundred death-dedicated troops, cut the cliff face and climbed like monkeys on ropes; toe and crown touching, by dawn they reached the tower and in one surge entered, annihilating all defending rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Hailancha led six hundred picked men who scaled the cliff face on ropes, toe to heel, reached the tower at dawn, and stormed in, slaughtering the entire garrison.

sentences.zh: 數十里賊寨聞之皆奪氣，悉破之，乘勝臨遜克宗壘。

translations.literal: Rebel stockades for several tens of li, hearing of it, all lost spirit; all were broken; pressing the victory they came before the fortress of Xunkezong.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel posts for miles around lost heart, fell one after another, and the victors pressed on to the fortress of Xunkezong.

sentences.zh: 索諾木酖殺僧格桑而獻其屍，及其妻妾頭目，至軍乞赦己罪。

translations.literal: Suonuomu poisoned and killed Senggesang and presented his corpse, together with his wives, concubines, and chiefs, coming to the army to beg pardon for his own crime.
translations.idiomatic: Suonuomu poisoned Senggesang and brought his corpse, along with his wives, concubines, and chiefs, to the camp to plead for his own life.

sentences.zh: 阿桂檻送京師。

translations.literal: Agui sent him to the capital in a cangue.
translations.idiomatic: Agui sent him to the capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 四十年四月，阿桂先使福康安、海蘭察赴河西助明亮攻宜喜，遂分兵六路，盡滅河西二十里內之賊。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fortieth year Agui first sent Fukang'an and Hailancha west of the river to aid Mingliang in attacking Yixi, then divided troops into six routes and utterly destroyed the rebels within twenty li west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Qianlong 40 (1775) Agui sent Fukang'an and Hailancha west of the river to help Mingliang at Yixi, then split his force into six columns and cleared the rebels from twenty li of the west bank.

sentences.zh: 五月，阿桂河東之軍破朗噶寨，距勒烏圍僅數里，環營進逼其巢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Agui's army east of the river broke Langga stockade, only several li from Lewuwei, encircling camps and pressing forward on their nest.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Agui's eastern force took Langga stockade, only a few li from Lewuwei, and ringed the rebel stronghold with camps.

sentences.zh: 七月，抵勒烏圍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month they reached Lewuwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they reached Lewuwei.

sentences.zh: 八月十五夜，進搗賊巢，四面砲轟官寨，破之。

translations.literal: On the night of the fifteenth of the eighth month they advanced to storm the rebel nest; cannon on all four sides bombarded the official stockade and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the Mid-Autumn Festival they assaulted the rebel nest; cannon fire from all sides shattered the chief stockade.

sentences.zh: 黎明，克轉經樓，逸賊皆溺水死。

translations.literal: At dawn they took the sutra-turning hall; fleeing rebels all drowned.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they seized the prayer hall; fleeing rebels drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 莎羅奔兄弟及各頭目已先期遁往噶爾崖。

translations.literal: Suoluo Ben's brothers and the various chiefs had already fled beforehand to Ga'erya.
translations.idiomatic: Suoluo Ben's kin and the rebel chiefs had already slipped away to Ga'erya.

sentences.zh: 十一月，官軍攻克科布曲山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the government army took Mount Kebuqu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month government forces took Mount Kebuqu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遂據瑪爾古山，噶爾崖即在其下。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they then occupied Mount Ma'ergu; Ga'erya lay directly below it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they seized Mount Ma'ergu, with Ga'erya directly beneath them.

sentences.zh: 索諾木之母姑姊妹亦降。

translations.literal: Suonuomu's mother, paternal aunts, and sisters also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Suonuomu's mother, aunts, and sisters surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 官軍三路合圍噶爾崖，斷其水道。

translations.literal: The government army on three routes jointly encircled Ga'erya and cut off its water supply.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces converged on Ga'erya from three directions and cut off its water.

sentences.zh: 索諾木使其兄詣營乞哀，不允。

translations.literal: Suonuomu sent his elder brother to the camp to beg for mercy; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Suonuomu sent his brother to plead for mercy at the camp; the plea was refused.

sentences.zh: 圍攻益急，索諾木從莎羅奔及其妻子挈番眾二千餘出寨，奉印獻軍門降，金川平。

translations.literal: The siege grew fiercer; Suonuomu followed Suoluo Ben and his wife and children, leading more than two thousand tribesmen out of the stockade, presented the seal and surrendered at the army gate; Jinchuan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege tightened, Suonuomu followed Suoluo Ben and his family out with more than two thousand tribesmen, surrendered the seal at headquarters, and Jinchuan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 四十一年正月，獻俘廟社，封賞阿桂等，勒碑太學，並及兩金川。

translations.literal: In the first month of the forty-first year captives were presented at the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain; Agui and others were enfeoffed and rewarded; a stele was carved at the Imperial Academy, extending to both Jinchuans.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianlong 41 the captives were presented at the state temples, Agui and his colleagues were rewarded, and a commemorative stele was erected at the Imperial Academy honoring the pacification of both Jinchuans.

sentences.zh: 旋於大金川設阿爾古廳，小金川設美諾廳。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter the A'ergu subprefecture was established in Greater Jinchuan and the Meinuo subprefecture in Lesser Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Greater Jinchuan was organized as the A'ergu subprefecture and Lesser Jinchuan as the Meinuo subprefecture.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，並阿爾古入美諾，改為懋功廳。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year A'ergu was merged into Meinuo and renamed the Maogong subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 44 the two districts were merged into the Maogong subprefecture.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，粵匪石達開竄寧遠，假道卭部土司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi the Cantonese rebel Shi Dakai fled into Ningyuan, taking passage through the Qiongbu native chieftain's territory.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 2 the Taiping commander Shi Dakai fled into Ningyuan by way of the Qiongbu chieftain's domain.

sentences.zh: 土司先受官軍約束，引賊至紫打地。

translations.literal: The native chieftain had first accepted government army instructions and led the rebels to Zida.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain, acting on government orders, lured the rebels to Zida.

sentences.zh: 四面阻絕，達開糧罄路窮，射書千戶王應元買路，復使人說土司嶺承恩求緩兵，皆不應，日殺馬煮桑葉為食。

translations.literal: Blocked on all four sides, Dakai's grain was exhausted and his roads cut off; he shot a letter to Battalion Commander Wang Yingyuan offering to buy a passage, and again sent men to persuade the native chieftain Ling Chengen to seek a respite in fighting—all were refused; daily they killed horses and boiled mulberry leaves for food.
translations.idiomatic: Surrounded on every side, Dakai ran out of food and escape routes; he sent word offering Wang Yingyuan a bribe for safe passage and asked Chieftain Ling Chengen to intercede for a truce, but both pleas were refused. His men killed horses and boiled mulberry leaves to survive.

sentences.zh: 四月，承恩、應元等偵賊力竭，率夷眾蹙攻，擒達開並賊官五人付官軍，檻送成都，四川總督駱秉章誅之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Chengen, Yingyuan, and the others, detecting that the rebels' strength was spent, led tribal masses in pressing attack, captured Dakai together with five rebel officials and handed them to the government army, sent them in cangues to Chengdu, and Sichuan Governor-General Luo Bingzhang executed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Chengen and Yingyuan, seeing the rebels exhausted, led tribal levies in a final assault, captured Dakai and five of his officers, and delivered them to government troops for transport to Chengdu, where Governor-General Luo Bingzhang had them executed.

sentences.zh: 奏加承恩、應元二品銜，賊軍錙重悉為兩土司所得。

translations.literal: A memorial was submitted to add second-rank titles for Chengen and Yingyuan; all the rebel army's baggage and heavy goods were obtained by the two native chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Chengen and Yingyuan were recommended for second-rank honors; the two chieftains took all the rebel army's supplies as spoil.

sentences.zh: 初，瞻對土司恃強不法，雍正八年，四川提督黃廷桂剿降之。

translations.literal: At first the Drayak native chieftain relied on strength and acted lawlessly; in the eighth year of Yongzheng Sichuan Provincial Commander Huang Tinggui campaigned and reduced him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Drayak chieftain had grown lawless through sheer force; in Yongzhi 8 Provincial Commander Huang Tinggui subdued him by arms.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年，四川提督李質粹等率兵五千，取道東俄落，至裏塘進兵，連破番寨，獲賊首噶籠丹坪。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong Sichuan Provincial Commander Li Zhicui and others led five thousand troops, took the route through Dong'eluo, advanced from Litang, broke barbarian stockades in succession, and captured the rebel leader Galong Danping.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 10 Li Zhicui led five thousand men through Dong'eluo and advanced from Litang, storming stockade after stockade and capturing the rebel leader Galong Danping.

sentences.zh: 十一年，質粹會欽差大臣班第，統兵進克泥日寨，燒斃番酋薑錯太，撫定丫魯、下密等處番夷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Zhicui joined Imperial Commissioner Bandi, commanded troops in advance to take Niri stockade, burned and killed the barbarian chieftain Jiangcuotai, and pacified the barbarian tribes at Yalu, Xiami, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhicui joined Imperial Commissioner Bandi, took Niri stockade, killed the chieftain Jiangcuotai in the fighting, and pacified the tribes of Yalu, Xiami, and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年，中瞻對土司洛布七力劫掠鄰番，抗捕傷兵。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing the Central Drayak native chieftain Luobuqili plundered neighboring tribes, resisted arrest, and wounded soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 19 the Central Drayak chieftain Luobuqili raided neighboring tribes, resisted arrest, and wounded government troops.

sentences.zh: 二十年，四川總督常明、提督多隆武領兵剿之，恃險死拒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Sichuan Governor-General Chang Ming and Provincial Commander Duolongwu led troops to suppress him; relying on difficult terrain he resisted to the death.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 20 Governor-General Chang Ming and Provincial Commander Duolongwu marched against him; he held the passes and fought to the last.

sentences.zh: 重慶鎮總兵羅思舉力戰破其巢，洛布七力焚死，分其地入上下瞻對。

translations.literal: Chongqing Garrison Regional Commander Luo Siju fought fiercely and broke his nest; Luobuqili burned to death; his territory was divided between Upper and Lower Drayak.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Luo Siju stormed his stronghold; Luobuqili died in the flames, and his domain was split between Upper and Lower Drayak.

sentences.zh: 洎咸豐中，土司工布朗結為人沉鷙，兼併上下瞻對之地，欲擁康部全境以抗川拒藏，鄰近各土司割地求免，貢賦唯命。

translations.literal: By the Xianfeng era the native chieftain Gongbulangjie was deep and fierce by nature; he annexed the lands of Upper and Lower Drayak, wished to hold the entire Kham region to resist Sichuan and repel Tibet, and neighboring native chieftains ceded territory to seek exemption, paying tribute and levies at his command.
translations.idiomatic: By the Xianfeng period Chieftain Gongbulangjie, a ruthless and cunning man, had absorbed Upper and Lower Drayak and aimed to dominate all of Kham against both Sichuan and Tibet. Neighboring chieftains ceded land to buy peace and paid tribute at his whim.

sentences.zh: 至是藏人怒，求四川出兵，秉章派道員史致康率師會藏進討。

translations.literal: At this the Tibetans were enraged and asked Sichuan to send troops; Bingzhang dispatched Circuit Intendant Shi Zhikang to lead an army and join Tibet in advancing to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans, enraged, appealed to Sichuan for troops; Bingzhang sent Circuit Intendant Shi Zhikang to join them in a punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 致康怯，頓打箭爐久，藏番需茶急，馳兵克之，殺工布朗結父子，致康始逡巡至。

translations.literal: Zhikang was timid and halted at Dajianlu for a long time; the Tibetan tribes urgently needed tea, rushed troops and took it, killed Gongbulangjie and his son; only then did Zhikang slowly arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhikang, timid by nature, lingered at Dajianlu while the Tibetans, desperate for tea, rushed in and killed Gongbulangjie and his son; only then did Zhikang belatedly appear.

sentences.zh: 藏人索兵費銀十六萬兩，秉章未允，藏人因據其地，設官兵駐守。

translations.literal: The Tibetans demanded one hundred sixty thousand taels of silver for military expenses; Bingzhang did not agree; the Tibetans therefore occupied the territory and stationed government troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans demanded 160,000 taels in war costs; Bingzhang refused, and they occupied the region and garrisoned it with their own troops.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，丁寶楨為四川總督，以瞻對藏官虐民，往往激變，每歲派員帶兵出關彈壓。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu Ding Baozhen was governor-general of Sichuan; because Drayak Tibetan officials oppressed the people, disturbances often broke out, and each year officials were dispatched with troops beyond the pass to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu reign Governor-General Ding Baozhen found that Tibetan officials in Drayak oppressed the people and provoked frequent unrest, and each year he sent troops beyond the frontier passes to restore order.

sentences.zh: 劉秉璋繼之，稍寬縱，藏官益驕橫。

translations.literal: Liu Bingzhang succeeded him and was somewhat lenient and indulgent; Tibetan officials grew even more arrogant and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: His successor Liu Bingzhang was more lenient, and the Tibetan officials grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 各土司多被威脅，唯明正土司地大，不之服，頻年爭鬥。

translations.literal: Most native chieftains were intimidated; only the Mingzheng native chieftain, whose territory was large, would not submit, and year after year they fought.
translations.idiomatic: Most chieftains were cowed into submission; only Mingzheng, with its large domain, refused to yield, and fighting broke out year after year.

sentences.zh: 十五年，瞻對內訌，逐藏官，乞內附，秉璋不許，唯治番官及亂民數人罪，由藏易官，且添駐堪布一人，兵八百名助守。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Drayak had internal strife, expelled Tibetan officials, and begged to be annexed inward; Bingzhang did not permit it, only punished a few barbarian officials and disorderly people, replaced officials through Tibet, and moreover added one stationed khenpo and eight hundred troops to assist in garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 15 civil strife in Drayak drove out the Tibetan officials, who petitioned to come under direct Chinese rule. Bingzhang refused annexation, punished only a few ringleaders, replaced the Tibetan administration, and posted an additional khenpo with eight hundred troops.

sentences.zh: 二十年，硃窩、章谷土司爭襲滋事，瞻對番官率兵越境干預，開槍傷我官兵。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the Zhuyao and Zhanggu native chieftains disputed succession and stirred up trouble; Drayak barbarian officials led troops across the border to intervene and opened fire, wounding our government troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 20 succession disputes at Zhuyao and Zhanggu drew in Drayak Tibetan officials, who crossed the border with troops and fired on Chinese soldiers.

sentences.zh: 四川總督鹿傳霖奏瞻對為蜀門戶，宜設法收回內屬，派提督周萬順、知縣張繼率兵出關，擊敗番兵，不三月，克瞻對並德爾格忒即疊蓋。

translations.literal: Sichuan Governor-General Lu Chuanlin memorialized that Drayak was the gateway of Shu and should be recovered for inner attachment by every means; he dispatched Provincial Commander Zhou Wanshun and Magistrate Zhang Ji to lead troops beyond the pass, defeated barbarian troops, and in less than three months took Drayak and Dege, namely Derge.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Lu Chuanlin argued that Drayak was the gateway to Sichuan and must be brought back under direct rule. He sent Provincial Commander Zhou Wanshun and Magistrate Zhang Ji beyond the passes; within three months they defeated the Tibetan forces and took both Drayak and Derge.

sentences.zh: 舊名保蓋。

translations.literal: Its old name was Baogai.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly known as Baogai.

sentences.zh: 全境，擒德格土司夫婦，解至成都，議敘改設流官。

translations.literal: the entire territory; captured the Dege native chieftain and his wife, sent them to Chengdu, and deliberated on replacing the post with a regular official.
translations.idiomatic: The whole region was secured, the Dege chieftain and his wife were captured and sent to Chengdu, and plans were drawn up to replace native rule with regular officials.

sentences.zh: 成都將軍恭壽憤傳霖不先會商，結駐藏大臣文海，密奏劾傳霖，翻原案，復德格土司職，仍以瞻對屬藏。

translations.literal: Chengdu General Gong Shou, angered that Chuanlin had not consulted beforehand, joined with the Resident Commissioner in Tibet Wenhain a secret memorial impeaching Chuanlin, reversed the original case, restored the Dege native chieftain's office, and still left Drayak under Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu General Gong Shou, furious that Chuanlin had not consulted him, joined Tibet's Resident Commissioner Wenhain a secret impeachment that reversed the decision, restored the Dege chieftain, and left Drayak under Tibetan jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 三十一年春，駐藏大臣鳳全被戕於巴塘，四川總督錫良奏請以四川提督馬維騏、建昌道趙爾豐進討。

translations.literal: In spring of the thirty-first year the Resident Commissioner in Tibet Feng Quan was killed at Batang; Sichuan Governor-General Xiliang memorialized requesting Sichuan Provincial Commander Ma Weiqi and Jianchang Circuit Intendant Zhao Erfeng to advance in punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Guangxu 31 Resident Commissioner Feng Quan was murdered at Batang; Governor-General Xiliang recommended Provincial Commander Ma Weiqi and Circuit Intendant Zhao Erfeng for a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 維騏率師先發。

translations.literal: Weiqi led the army in setting out first.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqi marched out first with the main force.

sentences.zh: 先是泰凝寺產沙金，錫良准商人採辦，幷派兵彈壓。

translations.literal: Earlier the Taining Monastery produced placer gold; Xiliang permitted merchants to undertake mining and also dispatched troops to suppress disturbances.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, placer gold had been found at Taining Monastery; Xiliang licensed merchant mining and sent troops to keep order.

sentences.zh: 寺中喇嘛反抗，殺都司盧鳴颺，瞻對潛助其亂，維騏出關討平之。

translations.literal: Lamas in the monastery resisted, killed Battalion Commander Lu Mingyang; Drayak secretly aided their disorder; Weiqi went beyond the pass and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: The lamas resisted, killing Battalion Commander Lu Mingyang, with covert aid from Drayak; Weiqi crossed the frontier and suppressed the revolt.

sentences.zh: 六月，攻克巴塘，擒正土司羅進寶、副土司郭宗隆保，誅之，移其妻子於成都安置。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Batang was taken by storm; the principal native chieftain Luo Jinbao and deputy chieftain Guo Zonglongbao were captured and executed; their wives and children were moved to Chengdu for resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Batang fell; Principal Chieftain Luo Jinbao and Deputy Chieftain Guo Zonglongbao were captured and executed, and their families were resettled in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 八月，爾豐至，殺堪布喇嘛及首惡數人祭鳳全。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Erfeng arrived, killed the khenpo lama and several chief villains as sacrifice to Feng Quan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Erfeng arrived and executed the khenpo and other ringleaders in retribution for Feng Quan's murder.

sentences.zh: 維騏班師回，爾豐接辦善後，派兵剿倡亂之七村溝，並搜捕餘匪，因移師討鄉城。

translations.literal: Weiqi withdrew the army and returned; Erfeng took over aftermath affairs, dispatched troops to suppress the Qicungou that had stirred rebellion, and searched out remaining bandits, then shifted the army to attack Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqi withdrew while Erfeng took over pacification, suppressed the rebel Qicungou district, hunted down stragglers, and then marched against Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 次年閏四月，克之，並攻克稻壩、貢噶嶺，一律肅清。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month of the following year it was taken, and Daoba and Gonggaling were also stormed and taken; all were thoroughly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month of the following year Xiangcheng fell, along with Daoba and Gonggaling, and the whole region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 於是爾豐建籌邊議，錫良以聞。

translations.literal: Thereupon Erfeng drafted proposals for frontier planning, and Xiliang reported them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Erfeng then drew up a frontier development plan, which Xiliang forwarded to the court.

sentences.zh: 朝廷特設督辦川滇邊務大臣，授爾豐。

translations.literal: The court specially established the post of Director-General of Sichuan-Yunnan Frontier Affairs and appointed Erfeng.
translations.idiomatic: The court created a special post of Director-General of Sichuan-Yunnan Frontier Affairs and gave it to Erfeng.

sentences.zh: 邊地在川、滇、甘、藏、青海間，縱橫各四五千里，土司居十之五，餘地歸呼圖克圖者十之一，清代賞藏者十之一，流為野番者十之三。

translations.literal: The frontier lay among Sichuan, Yunnan, Gansu, Tibet, and Qinghai, several thousand li in length and breadth; native chieftains held five-tenths, lands under khutukhtu one-tenth, lands granted by the Qing to Tibet one-tenth, and wild tribes three-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier belt between Sichuan, Yunnan, Gansu, Tibet, and Qinghai stretched thousands of li in every direction: native chieftains held half the land, khutukhtu domains a tenth, Qing grants to Tibet another tenth, and wild tribes the remaining three-tenths.

sentences.zh: 爾豐改巴塘、裏塘地設治，以所部防軍五營分駐之。

translations.literal: Erfeng reorganized Batang and Litang territories for administration, stationing his five garrison battalions among them.
translations.idiomatic: Erfeng established civil administration at Batang and Litang and garrisoned them with five battalions of frontier troops.

sentences.zh: 回川會商，錫良派道員趙淵出關坐鎮。

translations.literal: Returning to Sichuan for consultation, Xiliang dispatched Circuit Intendant Zhao Yuan beyond the pass to take command on site.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Sichuan for consultations, Xiliang sent Circuit Intendant Zhao Yuan beyond the passes to hold the frontier command.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，爾豐護理四川總督，奏准部撥開邊費銀一百萬兩。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year Erfeng acted as governor-general of Sichuan; a memorial was approved for the ministry to allocate one million taels of silver for frontier opening expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 33 Erfeng served as acting governor-general of Sichuan and secured ministry approval for one million taels in frontier development funds.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，授爾豐駐藏辦事大臣，仍兼邊務大臣，募西軍三營，率之出關。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year Erfeng was appointed Resident Commissioner in Tibet, still concurrently frontier affairs minister; he recruited three battalions of western troops and led them beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 34 he was named Resident Commissioner in Tibet while retaining his frontier post, raised three battalions of western troops, and marched out beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 時德格土司爭襲，構亂久，爾豐奏請往辦，經泰凝、道塢、章穀、倬倭、麻書、孔撒、白利、糸戎壩、擦玉龍、濯拉、擴洛垛以至更慶。

translations.literal: At that time the Dege native chieftainship disputed succession and had stirred disorder for long; Erfeng memorialized requesting to go handle it, passing through Taining, Daowu, Zhanggu, Zhuowai, Mashu, Kongsa, Baili, Sirongba, Cayulong, Zhuola, Kuoluoduo, reaching Gengqing.
translations.idiomatic: A long succession dispute at Dege was still unsettled; Erfeng petitioned to handle it in person, marching through Taining, Daowu, Zhanggu, and a chain of districts to Gengqing.

sentences.zh: 十二月，攻逆酋昂翁降白仁青等於贈科，匪竄雜渠卡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he attacked the rebel chiefs Angwengjiang Bailirenqing and others at Zengke; bandits fled to Zaqunka.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he defeated rebel chiefs including Angwengjiang Bailirenqing at Zengke; the survivors fled to Zaqunka.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年四月，攻雜渠卡。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Xuantong he attacked Zaqunka.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Xuantong 1 he assaulted Zaqunka.

sentences.zh: 五月，戰於麻木。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he fought at Maimu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he fought at Maimu.

sentences.zh: 六月，追匪十日程至卡納，一戰肅清，改流其地，並改春科、高日兩土司地及靈蔥土司之郎吉嶺村歸流。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he pursued bandits for ten days' march to Kana, cleared them in one battle, converted the territory to regular administration, and also converted the lands of the Chunke and Gaori native chieftains and the Langjiling village of the Lingcong native chieftain to regular rule.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he pursued the rebels for ten days to Kana and wiped them out in a single battle, converting the region to direct administration along with the domains of Chunke, Gaori, and the Langjiling district of Lingcong.

sentences.zh: 十月，四川兵入藏，藏番扼察木多以西地阻之，劫糧擄官。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Sichuan troops entered Tibet; Tibetan tribes held the lands west of Qamdo and blocked them, plundering grain and capturing officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Sichuan troops entered Tibet; Tibetan tribes west of Qamdo blocked their path, looted supplies, and seized officials.

sentences.zh: 爾豐率邊軍渡金沙江，逾雪山，抵察木多，送川兵行，於是三十九族、波密、八宿均請附邊轄。

translations.literal: Erfeng led frontier troops across the Jinsha River, over snow mountains, reached Qamdo, and escorted the Sichuan troops onward; thereupon the Thirty-Nine Clans, Bomi, and Basu all requested attachment to frontier jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Erfeng led frontier troops across the Jinsha and over the snow ranges to Qamdo, cleared the way for the Sichuan column, and the Thirty-Nine Clans, Bomi, and Basu all petitioned to come under frontier administration.

sentences.zh: 三十九族者：曰夥爾，曰圖嘛魯，曰吉寧塔克，曰尼牙木查，曰松嘛巴，曰勒達克，曰多嘛巴，曰達爾羊巴，曰他瑪，曰夥兒，曰拉寒，他瑪、夥兒、拉寒三族共一土司。

translations.literal: The Thirty-Nine Clans were: called Huo'er, Tumalu, Jiningtaka, Niyamucha, Songmaba, Ledake, Duomaba, Da'eryangba, Tama, Huo'er, Lahan—Tama, Huo'er, and Lahan three clans sharing one native chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: The Thirty-Nine Clans included Huo'er, Tumalu, Jiningtaka, Niyamucha, Songmaba, Ledake, Duomaba, Da'eryangba, and Tama, Huo'er, and Lahan—the last three sharing a single chieftain.

sentences.zh: 曰夥耳，曰瓊布噶，曰瓊布色爾查，曰瓊布納克魯，曰紮瑪爾，曰上阿紮，曰下阿紮，曰上奪爾樹，曰下奪爾樹，曰上剛噶爾，曰下剛噶爾，曰他瑪爾，曰提瑪爾，曰枳多，曰哇拉，枳多、哇拉二族共一土司。

translations.literal: called Huo'er, Qiongbuga, Qiongbuse'ercha, Qiongbumakelu, Zha'ma'er, Shang'azha, Xia'azha, Shangduo'ershu, Xiaduo'ershu, Shanggangga'er, Xiagangga'er, Tamar, Timar, Zhiduo, Wala—Zhiduo and Wala two clans sharing one native chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Also Huo'er, Qiongbuga, Qiongbuse'ercha, Qiongbumakelu, Zha'ma'er, Upper and Lower Azha, Upper and Lower Duo'ershu, Upper and Lower Gangga'er, Tamar, Timar, and Zhiduo and Wala—the last two under one chieftain.

sentences.zh: 曰麻弄，曰布川目桑，曰書達格魯克，曰奔盆，曰策令畢魯，曰色爾查，曰納布貢巴，曰結拉克汁，曰拉巴，曰三渣，曰朴樸，皆自為部落。

translations.literal: called Manong, Buchuanmusang, Shudageluke, Benpen, Celingbilu, Se'ercha, Nabugongba, Jielakezhi, Laba, Sanzha, Pupu—all were tribes in their own right.
translations.idiomatic: Also Manong, Buchuanmusang, Shudageluke, Benpen, Celingbilu, Se'ercha, Nabugongba, Jielakezhi, Laba, Sanzha, and Pupu—each an independent tribe.

sentences.zh: 設土總百戶或土百戶、土百長等以治之，歸駐藏大臣管轄。

translations.literal: Native general headmen of hundreds, native headmen of hundreds, or native hundred-chiefs and the like were established to govern them, under the jurisdiction of the Resident Commissioner in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: They were governed through native headmen of various ranks, all under the Resident Commissioner in Tibet.

sentences.zh: 爾豐以其族素恭順，悉加慰遣；

translations.literal: Erfeng, because these clans had always been respectful and obedient, comforted and dismissed them all;
translations.idiomatic: Erfeng, finding them habitually loyal, reassured each clan in turn;

sentences.zh: 因派兵剿類伍齊、碩搬多、洛隆宗、邊壩等阻路之番人，又分兵取江卡、貢覺、桑昂、雜瑜，咸收服之。

translations.literal: then dispatched troops to suppress the tribes blocking the road at Leiwuqi, Shuobanduo, Luolongzong, Bianba, and elsewhere, and also divided troops to take Jiangka, Gongjue, Sang'ang, and Zayu—all were received in submission.
translations.idiomatic: then sent columns against tribes blocking the routes at Leiwuqi, Shuobanduo, Luolongzong, and Bianba, and detached forces to take Jiangka, Gongjue, Sang'ang, and Zayu—all of which submitted.

sentences.zh: 二年，邊軍直抵江達，爾豐奏請以江達為邊藏分界。

translations.literal: In the second year frontier troops reached Jiangda directly; Erfeng memorialized requesting that Jiangda be the border between frontier and Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 2 frontier troops reached Jiangda, and Erfeng proposed making it the boundary between the frontier administration and Tibet.

sentences.zh: 五月，邊軍返察木多。

translations.literal: In the fifth month frontier troops returned to Qamdo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the frontier army withdrew to Qamdo.

sentences.zh: 六月，爾豐率兵略乍丫地。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Erfeng led troops to survey the Chaya region.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Erfeng led a reconnaissance into the Chaya region.

sentences.zh: 八月，巡阿足返，設乍丫委員。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, after patrolling Azu and returning, a Chaya commissioner was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, after a tour through Azu, he established a Chaya commissioner.

sentences.zh: 聞定鄉兵變，派統領鳳山追剿。

translations.literal: Hearing of a military mutiny at Dingxiang, he dispatched Commander Fengshan to pursue and suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: On news of a mutiny at Dingxiang he sent Commander Fengshan in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 九月，三岩野番投書索戰，爾豐率兵赴貢覺。

translations.literal: In the ninth month wild tribes of Sanyan sent a letter demanding battle; Erfeng led troops to Gongjue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the wild tribes of Sanyan sent a challenge; Erfeng marched to Gongjue.

sentences.zh: 十月，派傅嵩矞攻三岩，一旬而克。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he dispatched Fu Songyu to attack Sanyan; it was taken in ten days.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he sent Fu Songyu against Sanyan, which fell within ten days.

sentences.zh: 十一月，設三岩委員。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month a Sanyan commissioner was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month a Sanyan commissioner was appointed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，設貢覺委員。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month a Gongjue commissioner was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month a Gongjue commissioner was appointed.

sentences.zh: 爾豐旋返巴塘。

translations.literal: Erfeng soon returned to Batang.
translations.idiomatic: Erfeng then returned to Batang.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，爾豐以巴塘所屬之得榮浪藏寺數年不服，派兵攻克之，設得榮委員，並收服冷卡石。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year Erfeng, because Derong Langzang Monastery under Batang had not submitted for several years, dispatched troops to storm it, established a Derong commissioner, and also received Lengkashi in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Xuantong 3 he stormed Derong Langzang Monastery, which had defied authority for years, appointed a Derong commissioner, and brought Lengkashi to heel.

sentences.zh: 三月，爾豐調任四川總督，四川布政使王人文繼之為邊務大臣。

translations.literal: In the third month Erfeng was transferred to be governor-general of Sichuan; Sichuan Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Renwen succeeded him as frontier affairs minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Erfeng was transferred to governor-general of Sichuan; Provincial Commissioner Wang Renwen succeeded him as frontier minister.

sentences.zh: 爾豐奏請人文未到任前，以嵩矞代理。

translations.literal: Erfeng memorialized requesting that before Renwen took office Songyu act as agent.
translations.idiomatic: Erfeng asked that Songyu serve as acting minister until Renwen arrived.

sentences.zh: 四月，同發巴塘，至孔撒、麻書，設甘孜委員，檄靈蔥、白利、倬倭、東科、單東、魚科、明正、魚通各土司繳印，改土歸流。

translations.literal: In the fourth month they set out together from Batang, reached Kongsa and Mashu, established a Garze commissioner, and ordered the native chieftains of Lingcong, Baili, Zhuowai, Dongke, Dandong, Yukex, Mingzheng, and Yutong to surrender their seals and convert from native rule to regular administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month they marched from Batang through Kongsa and Mashu, set up a Garze commissioner, and ordered the chieftains of Lingcong, Baili, Zhuowai, Dongke, Dandong, Yukex, Mingzheng, and Yutong to surrender their seals for conversion to direct rule.

sentences.zh: 色達及上羅科野番來歸。

translations.literal: Seda and the wild tribes of Shangluoke came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Seda and the wild tribes of Shangluoke submitted.

sentences.zh: 適駐藏大臣聯豫電請邊軍攻波密，因奏派副都統鳳山率兵二千往應。

translations.literal: Just then the Resident Commissioner in Tibet Lianyu telegraphed requesting frontier troops to attack Bomi; a memorial was therefore submitted dispatching Vice Commander-in-Chief Fengshan with two thousand troops to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Resident Commissioner Lianyu then telegraphed for frontier troops against Bomi, and Fengshan was sent with two thousand men in response.

sentences.zh: 六月，爾豐至瞻對，藏官逃，收其地，設瞻對委員。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Erfeng reached Drayak; Tibetan officials fled; he recovered the territory and established a Drayak commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Erfeng reached Drayak; the Tibetan officials fled, and he took the district and appointed a Drayak commissioner.

sentences.zh: 旋經道塢、打箭爐，檄魚通、卓斯各土司繳印改流。

translations.literal: Soon he passed through Daowu and Dajianlu, ordering the native chieftains of Yutong, Zhuosi, and others to surrender seals and convert to regular administration.
translations.idiomatic: He then passed through Daowu and Dajianlu and ordered the Yutong, Zhuosi, and other chieftains to surrender their seals for conversion to direct rule.

sentences.zh: 爾豐入川，沿途收咱里、冷邊、沈邊三土司印，嵩矞復出關改流泰凝，而魚科土司結下羅科抗命。

translations.literal: Erfeng entered Sichuan, along the way collecting the seals of the three native chieftains Zali, Lengbian, and Shenbian; Songyu again went beyond the pass to convert Taining to regular rule, while the Yukex native chieftain joined Xialuoke in resisting orders.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Sichuan, Erfeng collected seals from the Zali, Lengbian, and Shenbian chieftains; Songyu again crossed the passes to convert Taining, while the Yukex chieftain allied with Xialuoke in open defiance.

sentences.zh: 嵩矞令上羅科扼其險，擊平之，斃魚科土司，於是嵩矞奏請設西康省，而沃日、崇喜、納奪、革伯咱、巴底、巴旺、靈蔥、上納奪各土司，暨乍丫、察木多兩呼圖克圖，相繼繳印。

translations.literal: Songyu ordered Shangluoke to hold the strategic passes, attacked and pacified them, killed the Yukex native chieftain; thereupon Songyu memorialized requesting establishment of Xikang Province, while the native chieftains of Wori, Chongxi, Naduo, Geboizai, Badi, Bawang, Lingcong, and Shangnaduo, together with the two khutukhtu of Chaya and Qamdo, surrendered their seals in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Songyu had Shangluoke hold the defiles, crushed the rebels, and killed the Yukex chieftain; he then memorialized for the creation of Xikang Province, and the chieftains of Wori, Chongxi, Naduo, Geboizai, Badi, Bawang, Lingcong, and Shangnaduo, with the Chaya and Qamdo khutukhtu, surrendered their seals one after another.

sentences.zh: 惟毛丫、曲登乞緩，許之。

translations.literal: Only Maoya and Qudeng begged for delay, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Only Maoya and Qudeng asked for more time, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 涼山夷倮儸者，居寧遠、越巂、峨邊、雷波、馬邊間，淺山部落頭目屬於土司。

translations.literal: The Liangshan Yi Nuosu dwelt among Ningyuan, Yuexi, Ebian, Leibo, and Mabian; chiefs of shallow-mountain tribes were subordinate to native chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: The Nuosu Yi of Liangshan lived among Ningyuan, Yuexi, Ebian, Leibo, and Mabian; chiefs of the lower hills were subject to native chieftains.

sentences.zh: 深入則涼山，數百里皆夷地。

translations.literal: Going deeper one reached Liangshan; for several hundred li all was Yi territory.
translations.idiomatic: Farther in lay Liangshan itself, hundreds of li of Yi country.

sentences.zh: 生夷黑骨頭為貴種，白骨頭者曰熟夷，執賤役。

translations.literal: Among raw Yi, black bones were the noble caste; white bones were called cooked Yi and performed menial service.
translations.idiomatic: Among the 'raw' Yi, those of the black-bone caste were nobles; white-bone 'cooked' Yi performed menial labor.

sentences.zh: 夷族分數百支，不相統屬。

translations.literal: The Yi were divided into several hundred branches and were not under unified authority.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi were split into hundreds of branches under no common authority.

sentences.zh: 叛則出掠，擄漢民作奴，遇兵散匿。

translations.literal: When they rebelled they went out to plunder, captured Han people as slaves, and when troops came they scattered and hid.
translations.idiomatic: In revolt they raided the lowlands, enslaved Han captives, and melted away when troops appeared.

sentences.zh: 清興，雍正五年、七年，嘉慶十三年、十六年，迭經川吏剿撫，加以部勒。

translations.literal: Since the rise of the Qing, in the fifth and seventh years of Yongzheng, the thirteenth and sixteenth years of Jiaqing, Sichuan officials repeatedly campaigned and pacified them, imposing discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Qing rise, Sichuan officials had campaigned against them in Yongzhi 5 and 7 and Jiaqing 13 and 16, alternately fighting and conciliating.

sentences.zh: 同治末，越巂夷叛，成都將軍崇實兼攝四川總督，奏調貴州提督周達武率軍由陝回剿，前鋒羅應旒出清溪，撫大樹堡、左右王嶺各土司，進駐保安，攻降洽馬里、阿波落、跑馬坪、燕麥廠，遂克普雄石城，夷地四百里間咸受約束。

translations.literal: At the end of Tongzhi the Yuexi Yi rebelled; Chengdu General Chong Shi, also acting as governor-general of Sichuan, memorialized transferring Guizhou Provincial Commander Zhou Dawu to lead troops returning from Shaanxi in suppression; vanguard Luo Yingliu went out from Qingxi, pacified the native chieftains of Dashubao and Zuoyou Wangling, advanced and encamped at Bao'an, attacked and reduced Qiamali, Aboluo, Paomaping, and Yanmaichang, then took Puxiong Stone City; within four hundred li of Yi territory all were brought under constraint.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tongzhi the Yuexi Yi rebelled; Chengdu General Chong Shi, acting as governor-general, called in Guizhou Provincial Commander Zhou Dawu from the Shaanxi campaign. Vanguard Luo Yingliu advanced from Qingxi, won over the Dashubao and Wangling chieftains, encamped at Bao'an, and reduced Qiamali, Aboluo, Paomaping, and Yanmaichang before taking Puxiong Stone City, bringing four hundred li of Yi country under control.

sentences.zh: 官軍至靖遠，刷茲、林加、布約、尼錢、交腳等支亦降，更設靖遠新老兩營土千百戶，出漢奴數萬。

translations.literal: When government troops reached Jingyuan, the branches Shazi, Linjia, Buyue, Niqian, Jiaojiao, and others also surrendered; new and old Jingyuan battalion native chiefs of thousands and hundreds were further established, and tens of thousands of Han slaves were released.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingyuan the Shazi, Linjia, Buyue, Niqian, and Jiaojiao branches submitted as well; new native headmen were installed and tens of thousands of Han slaves were freed.

sentences.zh: 迨爾豐經營關外，朝廷以其兄爾巽督川，爾巽欲悉平涼山夷以利邊務，光緒三十四年八月，派建昌鎮總兵鳳山、建昌道馬汝驥等，率兵暨民團剿寧遠吉狄、馬加、拉斯等支倮夷。

translations.literal: When Erfeng was developing affairs beyond the pass, the court had his elder brother Erxun supervise Sichuan; Erxun wished to pacify all Liangshan Yi to benefit frontier affairs; in the eighth month of the thirty-fourth year of Guangxu he dispatched Jianchang Garrison Regional Commander Fengshan, Jianchang Circuit Intendant Ma Ruji, and others to lead troops and militia in suppressing the Nuosu branches Jidi, Majia, Lasi, and others of Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: While Erfeng developed the frontier, his brother Erxun governed Sichuan and sought to pacify all of Liangshan for the border enterprise. In Guangxu 34 he sent Regional Commander Fengshan and Circuit Intendant Ma Ruji with troops and militia against the Jidi, Majia, Lasi, and other Nuosu branches of Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 進至里足山梁，旋值國喪，罷兵。

translations.literal: They advanced to Lizu Mountain Ridge; soon the nation mourned and troops were halted.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Lizu Mountain Ridge, but the campaign was halted when the court went into mourning for the emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年正月，令建昌鎮總兵田鎮邦、甯遠府知府陳廷緒再舉，征服淺山白母子、嗎噠拉施、三合等支，並收撫咱雞租、五支、別牛、租租等支，於是加拉及吉狄、馬加等支先後降。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xuantong Jianchang Garrison Regional Commander Tian Zhenbang and Ningyuan Prefect Chen Tingxu were ordered to campaign again; they conquered the shallow-mountain branches Baimuzi, Madalashi, Sanhe, and others, and also received and pacified the branches Zajizu, Wuzhi, Bieniu, Zuzu, and others; thereupon Jiala and the branches Jidi, Majia, and others surrendered in turn.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xuantong 1 Regional Commander Tian Zhenbang and Prefect Chen Tingxu resumed the campaign, subduing the Baimuzi, Madalashi, and Sanhe branches of the lower hills and winning over Zajizu, Wuzhi, Bieniu, and Zuzu; Jiala, Jidi, Majia, and others then submitted in succession.

sentences.zh: 官軍進駐交腳，收撫八切、阿什並阿落、馬家、上三支、下三支，野夷悉請內附，不隸土司。

translations.literal: Government troops advanced and encamped at Jiaojiao, received and pacified Baqie, Ashenbing, Aluo, Majia, Shang Sanzhi, and Xia Sanzhi; wild Yi all requested inner attachment and were not subordinate to native chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops encamped at Jiaojiao and brought in Baqie, Ashenbing, Aluo, Majia, and the upper and lower Sanzhi branches; wild Yi throughout the region petitioned for direct incorporation, no longer under chieftain rule.

sentences.zh: 先是馬邊夷阿侯蘇噶支戕英教士，拒捕，與馬邊協副將楊景昌軍相持。

translations.literal: Earlier the Mabian Yi Ahou Suga branch had killed an English missionary, resisted arrest, and faced off against the army of Mabian Assistant Regional Commander Yang Jingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Ahou Suga branch of Mabian had killed a British missionary and, resisting arrest, held off Assistant Regional Commander Yang Jingchang's troops.

sentences.zh: 爾巽調總兵董南斌往剿，與寧遠軍夾擊，阿侯蘇噶降。

translations.literal: Erxun transferred Regional Commander Dong Nanbin to go suppress them; together with the Ningyuan army they attacked from two sides, and Ahou Suga surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Erxun sent Regional Commander Dong Nanbin to join the Ningyuan force in a pincer attack, and Ahou Suga surrendered.

sentences.zh: 兩軍於十月二十五日貫通涼山夷巢，會於吽吽壩。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth of the tenth month the two armies pierced through the Liangshan Yi nest and met at Honghongba.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth of the tenth month the two columns linked up through the heart of Liangshan and met at Honghongba.

sentences.zh: 於是爾巽議禁黑夷蓄奴。

translations.literal: Thereupon Erxun deliberated on forbidding black-bone Yi from keeping slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Erxun then proposed banning slavery among the black-bone Yi nobility.

sentences.zh: 先就交腳設縣治，餘地擇要屯守；

translations.literal: First a county administration was established at Jiaojiao, and in remaining lands key points were chosen for garrison;
translations.idiomatic: A county seat was established at Jiaojiao and garrisons posted at strategic points elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 而西南由美姑河至雷波，辟雷寧通道四百餘里，駐兵守護，以通商旅。

translations.literal: southwest from the Meigu River to Leibo a Leining passage of more than four hundred li was opened, troops stationed to guard it, so merchants and travelers could pass.
translations.idiomatic: and a four-hundred-li route from the Meigu River to Leibo was opened and garrisoned to restore trade.

sentences.zh: 是役也，得地幾及千里，夷眾凡十餘萬人。

translations.literal: In this campaign territory gained was nearly a thousand li, and Yi masses totaled more than one hundred thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign brought nearly a thousand li of territory and more than one hundred thousand Yi under control.

sentences.zh: 二年，振邦、廷緒等師還討會理土司，披砂、會理村、苦竹、者保、通安舟等悉改流，至是川境土司多非舊觀矣。

translations.literal: In the second year Zhenbang, Tingxu, and the others withdrew their armies and attacked the Huili native chieftain; Pisha, Huilicun, Kuzhu, Zhebao, Tong'anzhou, and others were all converted to regular administration; by this time most native chieftains within Sichuan territory were no longer as they had been.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 2 Zhenbang and Tingxu turned to the Huili chieftain; Pisha, Huilicun, Kuzhu, Zhebao, and Tong'anzhou were all converted to direct rule, and native chieftain rule in Sichuan was largely a thing of the past.

sentences.zh: 今采傳世較永者著於篇。

translations.literal: Now those with comparatively longer surviving transmission are set forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Those with longer surviving records are set down in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 其國初歸附未久旋即絕滅者，尚不勝記云。

translations.literal: As for those who at the founding of the dynasty submitted but soon afterward were extinguished, they are too numerous even to record, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Those who submitted early in the dynasty but soon perished are too numerous to record.

sentences.zh: 拈佐阿革寨土百戶，系西番種類。

translations.literal: Niezuo Age Stockade native tusi of hundreds; of Western Tibetan stock.
